coinIcons.note: Transaction-type badges from the Figma "Coin Type" set. They take `size` but ignore `color` — their palette is raw hex from the file and does NOT follow the theme. Do not reach for these as general-purpose icons.

principles: Never use a raw hex, rgb(), or a primitive token (--gray-04) in product code. Always use a semantic token (--surface-tertiary). Primitives exist only to define semantics.
Semantic tokens are theme-reactive: the same token resolves light and dark automatically. Hardcoding a color breaks dark mode.
Compose from existing components before writing new markup. If a pattern needs a component that does not exist, flag it rather than hand-rolling a one-off.
Figma strokes take no layout space; CSS borders do. When a spec gives an explicit height AND a border, compensate the padding or draw the divider with an inset box-shadow.
Text sitting on a solid brand/status surface must use content-absolute-white, never a theme-reactive content token (it inverts in dark and disappears).

Table: Header row uses surface-secondary with a border-secondary underline; header cells are Subtitle/2 (500 weight), padding 16px 12px.
Body rows are surface-raised, 52px tall; cells are Body/2, padding 16px 8px.
Row hover is surface-secondary (grey); row selected is surface-brand-secondary (blue tint). They are DIFFERENT states — selected wins when both apply.
Container has a border-secondary 1px border, radius-mid (8px), and overflow:hidden to clip rows to the corners.
Dividers are inset box-shadows, not borders, so rows stay exactly 52px.
Three column modes, matching Figma's: `width={n}` is fixed; `width={n} fill` starts at n and grows, sharing spare space in proportion to the designed widths; omitting width gives an equal share.

Use `width={n} fill` for text columns — NOT a bare omitted width. Equal share gives every column the same size, so a long value like "Comprehensive ITR Filing" wraps and the row grows past its 52px. Reserve fixed widths for content that cannot reflow: the checkbox (40), a priority meter (80), a row of action icons.

Do not paste a Figma filter/table width onto every column as a fixed size. That is what stops a table being responsive at all — the columns cannot shrink, so they overflow and get clipped by the container.

A cell containing a checkbox is 40x52 with padding 12/8, in the header row and every body row alike — the component applies this on its own. Do not override it: the generic header (16/12) and body (16/8) paddings differ, which is what put the header checkbox 4px right of the column.
Button: Heights are 44 / 36 / 32 for large / medium / small; radius-sm (6px).
Icon-only is its own treatment (surface-raised + border-primary square 36/32/30 or circle 44/40/38), NOT the active variant squared off — pass the icon as children and always set aria-label.
Loading lightens the fill to the family's `subtle` step and disables interaction.
Secondary is the warning/orange family, not a grey — this is intentional in XUI.
Badge: Use the label-* variants for status and category pills; the accent-* variants are for softer inline tags.
Badges are 20px tall; the pill's border is included in that height.
Input: Two field heights, both from Figma: size="medium" is 48px (the library's Input_v2 field, the default) and size="small" is 44px (what the dashboard filter bar uses).
In a filter bar use size="small" so the search sits level with the 44px Selects beside it. At the 48px default it overhangs them by 4px.

Pass an icon to a Button with the iconLeft prop, never as a child — a child lands inside the label span and is laid out inline on the text baseline, which inflates the button past its 44/36/32 height and leaves the icon a couple of px above centre.
Select: `options` takes either a flat SelectOption[] or a SelectGroup[] ({ label, options }). Figma's panel (XUI file 583:4488) draws groups as a heading, its run of items, then a rule — pass groups and you get that; pass a flat list and you get one unnamed run.
An option carries more than a label: subLabel (quieter second line), icon or image on the left, rightIcon, disabled, and keywords to widen what search matches beyond the visible text.
The 32px left inset on every row is the space the check occupies on the selected one. It is held open deliberately so labels do not shift when the selection moves; `check={false}` removes both.
`searchInput` adds the filter field, with searchPlaceholder / emptySearchMessage / onSearchChange / clearSearchOnClose. A group whose options all filter out takes its heading with it.
`isClearable` swaps the chevron for a cross once a non-default value is chosen, and clearing returns to `defaultValue` rather than to nothing.

An option can carry its own `options` to nest one level deeper — Figma draws children bulleted and indented (Assets > Other Current Asset > Asset 123). Search keeps a parent when it matches OR when any descendant does, so a matching child is never orphaned.
`iconRight` replaces the trigger chevron; `optionItemRightIcon` puts a glyph at the end of every row that has no `rightIcon` of its own.

`isCustomOptionCreationAllowed` offers "+ Create New" when the typed text is not already an option — it is hidden for an exact match so the row never invites a duplicate. Handle it with `onCreateOption`, or let it fall through to `onChange`.
NOT built: virtualizeOptions, triggerButtonVariant and customCTAProps. The first changes how the list renders and the other two turn the trigger into a Button; both want their own pass.
In a filter bar every field FILLS the row in an equal share and only the trailing action hugs — this is the product's pattern (app.koinx.com/transactions). Do not give the fields fixed widths.
The 255px on Select is a flex BASIS, not a fixed width: drop a row of them into a flex container and they shrink to equal shares on their own, no per-field sizing needed.

Give every field in that row the SAME flex-basis. A field set to `flex: 1 1 0` next to Selects basing from 255px collapses to zero width once the row overflows, because shrink is distributed in proportion to basis.

Never wrap these in the pixel widths measured off a Figma filter bar. Those were 1-3px short of the placeholders they hold, so every label rendered an ellipsis. A label must never be the truncated text — it is the only thing saying what the control filters. Values may still ellipsise: a client name is unbounded.
A selected value renders in Subtitle/2 (500 weight), which is wider than the Body/2 placeholder — a box sized to fit the placeholder will clip the value once one is chosen.

`size` is Figma's Size axis on `select` (600:7833): `large` 44 (default) and `medium` 36. Medium is not merely shorter — its value line drops from 20 to 16, which is how Figma's own 10/12 padding lands on 36. Use medium in a filter bar.

Select IS the action menu — there is no separate Menu component and none is needed. `value={null}` keeps it controlled at nothing so the trigger never adopts what was picked (onChange becomes a dispatch, not a binding), and `check={false}` drops the tick and the 32px inset it reserves. Options already carry a left `icon`, a `rightIcon` and a `subLabel`.

`menuWidth` is 'trigger' by default — Figma's canvas shows menu width = trigger width for a Select FIELD. Pass 'content' for the action-menu case, where the trigger reads "Actions" and the rows are long enough to truncate against it: the panel then grows to its widest row, never narrower than the trigger, capped at 420. BEYOND FIGMA and additive — the drawn case is untouched.
EmptyState: Illustration, title, optional description, optional actions — centred in whatever box it is given, so a page-level 404 and an empty table cell use the same component.
Actions is a slot, not primaryAction/secondaryAction props: Figma's three screens use none, one and two buttons, and a slot covers all three.
Description is optional because Figma hides it on the "No Details Found" screen — pass nothing rather than an empty string.

Five parts: illustration, title, description, actions, footer. Only title is required, and an omitted part is dropped from the DOM rather than rendered empty, so the 37px rhythm closes up instead of leaving a hole.

`footer` is the "Tip: …" line under the actions. It is BEYOND the Figma screens — it exists so the component can express what KoinX's existing InfoComponent already ships. It renders quieter than the description (Subtitle/1 in content-tertiary); that pairing was chosen, not read from Figma.

`className` lands on the root; `classNames` (illustration / text / title / description / actions / footer) reaches the parts it cannot. Prefer neither — reach for them only when a screen genuinely needs to diverge.

Ship the illustrations from @koinx/xui (MaintenanceIllustration, ErrorIllustration, NoDataIllustration). Their paints are bound to the blue ramp, which is theme-reactive, so they render correctly on a dark page. A hand-pasted Figma SVG export will not — it arrives with the screen's white content card baked in and a pale backing circle that becomes a bright disc on black.
Dialog: Pass `icon` to get Figma's "Dialog with Icon" form (XUI file 1138:5672): a 64px glyph above the title, and the text centres.

Do not colour the icon yourself. The component colours it from the variant, read from Figma — default check_solid #0052FE (content-brand-primary), alert warning_amber #FB6F04 (content-warning-primary), destructive delete #F7324C (content-error-primary). Passing a pre-coloured icon is how a destructive dialog ends up with a blue trash can.
The two action buttons each fill half the row (flex: 1) with a 24px gap. Destructive puts the confirm button first; the other variants put cancel first.
Escape and a scrim click already close it, and `hideClose` removes the top-right X — no extra props needed for those.
Drawer: `placement` is right (default) / left / bottom / full. `bottom` is a sheet: it hugs its content up to 90vh rather than filling the screen, and rounds its corners at 16px.
`footer` is the call to action. Figma draws every placement both with and without one, so it is optional by design rather than by accident.
Escape, a scrim click and a body scroll-lock are already wired — do not reimplement them in a screen.

Geometry: panel padded 8 at the top, children 8 apart, 16px radius, a full-bleed rule under the header. The close control is a 32x32 box (XUI 1416:47417 draws `Icon / Close` at 32x32 in all eight frames) with a 24px glyph inside — that box, not the type, is what sets the header row height. The title is Subtitle/1, matching Figma's 22px text. Header and body both use 16px sides so the title shares a left edge with the body text. That 16 is a designer's call that OVERRIDES the file, which lays header content out at x=12; it is the one place this component knowingly departs from Figma. The footer's 16 is Figma's own.

Props beyond placement: `headingIcon` (a glyph before the title), `overlayBlur` (blurs the scrim, off by default, using --blur-locked), `width` (overrides the placement default; ignored by bottom and full), and `classNames` for titleWrapper / title / closeIcon / body / footer.

The footer is ALREADY pinned — it sits outside the scrolling body as flex:none. There is no separate "fixed bottom" mode to reach for; the library this mirrors splits that into variant strings, we get it from the layout.

`height` sets a fixed sheet height and lifts the default 90vh cap, so height="100%" really means full height. Beyond Figma (the file draws `bottom` hugging its content only) and approved: when the content outgrows the fixed height the body scrolls, because it is overflow-y:auto with min-height:0 while the header and footer are flex:none.

`draggable` (default true) swipes the panel away along its own axis — down for bottom, right for right, left for left. `full` never drags. Beyond Figma and approved. No gesture library. It yields where it should: a drag starting in a text field is ignored, and a scrollable body keeps the gesture until it is back at the top. Escape, scrim click and the close button work regardless.
Icons: Four tones: outlined, solid, dualtone, dualtone-selected. Outlined/solid inherit currentColor; dualtone defaults to content-tertiary and dualtone-selected to content-brand-primary.
Set --xui-icon-knockout to the surface an icon sits on if its cut-outs need to blend with something other than surface-raised.
Tabs: `size` is Figma's Size axis on `Tabs/Default` (1128:16648): `large` 42 (default) and `medium` 36. Medium drops the label to Subtitle/2 as well as trimming padding — that is how the item reaches 28, not padding alone.

The container was 44 until the variant-axis gate found the Size axis; 42 is Figma's number, and the 2px was a CSS border taking layout space where a Figma stroke does not. Its vertical padding is 3, not the 4 Figma draws, for that reason.

layoutPatterns.data table page: PageHeader (title + primary action) → filter/search toolbar → Table → Pagination. Selection surfaces a floating action bar.
layoutPatterns.form: Label above field, helper or error text below, 20px between fields; primary action bottom-right, secondary to its left.
layoutPatterns.empty state: Center a short message in a single full-width table cell using content-tertiary.

antiPatterns: Hardcoding #ffffff for a card background instead of surface-raised — it stays white in dark mode.
Using content-primary for a label on a brand-filled button — invisible in one of the two themes.
Adding a CSS border to a fixed-height element without shaving the padding — renders 2px taller than the spec.
Building a bespoke table with divs when Table/TableRow/TableCell already encode the spec.
Using surface-secondary for a selected row — that is the hover treatment; selected is surface-brand-secondary.

choosing.Switch vs Checkbox: Switch when choosing IS doing — it applies immediately. Checkbox when the value is collected and submitted with a form. If there is a Save button, it is a Checkbox.
choosing.Radio vs Dropdown: Radio shows every option at once: it costs vertical space and buys comparison. Past roughly five options, or when the options are not worth comparing, use Dropdown.
choosing.Tabs vs a form control: Tabs does not hold a value a form submits. If the selection changes what is displayed below it, it is Tabs; if it changes what will be saved, it is not.
choosing.Select vs Dropdown: Both pick one of many, and they are NOT variants of each other. Dropdown is the form field: label, mandatory, helperText, helperIcon, error. Select is the standalone picker for toolbars, filter bars and table controls: search, groups, one level of nesting, isClearable, and "+ Create New". If it needs a label and an error state it is Dropdown; if it needs search or groups it is Select.
choosing.PasswordInput vs SecretInput: Both mask, and that is all they share. A password is something the user knows and may have forgotten, so PasswordInput offers recovery. A secret is something the system issued and the user must read back, so SecretInput offers a reveal toggle. The wrong one gives an API-key field a "Forgot password?" link.
choosing.The Input family: There is one Input and seven specialisations — AmountInput, DateInput, PhoneInput, PasswordInput, SecretInput, Otp, FileUpload. Reach for the specialisation: each carries behaviour you would otherwise rebuild, and all of them share label / mandatory / helperText / helperIcon / error so they line up in a form.
choosing.Toast vs Dialog: A toast reports; a dialog asks. If the user has no choice to make, do not block them. Toast's single actionLabel/onAction is for undo, not for a decision.
choosing.Dialog vs Drawer: Length, not importance. Dialog when it fits without scrolling — a confirmation, a short form, a warning. Drawer when the content scrolls, or the user needs the page behind it in mind. On mobile placement="bottom" is the idiom for both; right is the desktop idiom.
choosing.Sidebar vs Tabs: Not alternatives. Sidebar moves between sections of the product; Tabs moves between views of the thing already being looked at. BottomNav is the mobile form of Sidebar, carrying the same destinations.
choosing.Badge vs PriorityMeter vs Toast vs Empty: Badge is a standing label on a thing (label-* for status and category pills, accent-* for softer inline tags). PriorityMeter is a level rather than a word, in a table column. Toast is a transient event. EmptyState is there being nothing to show.

status._comment: Per-component status, so a consumer can tell what is settled from what is still moving. A component absent from every list below matches Figma with nothing outstanding. Guides/Status renders this; keep it here rather than in prose so the page cannot drift.

openQuestions.question: The frame named "Left" in XUI 1416:47417 is drawn right-aligned — its panel sits at x=74 in a 390 screen, so it touches the right edge. `left` was built to mean left. Is the label the intent, or the drawing? They are one swap apart.

`full_height` in the library KoinX already uses is a right-hand panel at full height, which is what our `right` is. Our `full` spans both axes. On a phone the two look alike; on a desktop they do not. Which mapping was meant?

Two glyphs the product needs exist in no XUI library: an office building and a briefcase. (The magnifier, kebab and hamburger previously listed here DO exist — they were in the General Icon Library, not Icons v2, and now ship as SearchIcon, MoreVertIcon and MenuIcon.)
Guides > Choosing Components is editorial. Figma draws what a component looks like, not which to reach for, so those distinctions were written rather than read and want a designer's review pass.

XUI icons are monochrome across four tones. The ITR Filing chips use gradient-filled glyphs (the product file's own Dark/Gradients Orange / Blue / Pink styles), which no XUI tone can express. Either the system grows a gradient treatment or those chips take flat icons and lose the gradients.

The Figma "Coin Type" set (2441:12895) binds NO variables — all 369 fills are raw hex. Its palette (#4F677E disc, #26D0FF / #2AFF95 glyph) has no equivalent anywhere in the XUI ramp, so unlike Icons v2 these 48 badges do not follow the theme. Ship as fixed brand artwork, or bind the palette to tokens?
Three palette strays in the same set: #2BFF95 on 4 fills against #2AFF95 on 62 (one hex digit apart), and #1CD278 on 2. Almost certainly slips rather than intent.

Naming in the set: two components are both called "Dust", and there is a "Lost" beside a "Lost1". Code disambiguates the second Dust as DustCoin2 so the set can be generated at all; the file should be fixed rather than the workaround kept.

Category disagreements between Figma and xui.koinx.com: Spend, Liquidity Out and UnStake sit under Deposit in the set while the reference site lists Spend under Withdrawal; Mint and Burn are Expense in the set and Deposit/Withdrawal on the site. Code follows the Figma set. Also note the site's "CollatoralUnlockCoin" — the set spells it Collateral, which is what ships.

Five icons in the Icon Library are painted #FF0000 — Figma's default red — on glyphs with no reason to be red: Link, Realized Gains, a cog-transfer, a window-with-wrench, and two unnamed components. Every other icon in the library is monochrome, so this reads as a leftover override. They ship as drawn, which makes them obvious in Foundations > General Icons.

The library uses THREE different values for one monochrome: black, #0F172A (gray-12) and #334155 (gray-10). All three are mapped to currentColor so they behave identically, but the file should pick one.

Names reused inside the library for DIFFERENT drawings: Deposit (Arrows & controls vs Transactions), ArrowForward (Arrows vs File types), perm_device_information (Insights vs Communication). Plus exact duplicates: `cancel` twice and `Category` twice. The generator suffixes the later one; the fix is a rename.

Four components are not shipped and need a decision. `KoinX AI` is gradient-filled with a <use> transform, so it cannot be a currentColor glyph — same question as the coin chips. `Component 56` and `Component 57` carry Figma's default names, so there is nothing to call them. Five more are Iconify paste-ins that were renamed to what they draw (Spinner, BulletedList, Transaction Card, List Card, WindowSettings, SettingsTransfer) — worth confirming those names.

Figma defines variant axes for components XUI has not built at all: a Slider (Percentage), a select-shaped Select Date and Select Date Range (Size=[Large|Medium] — note these are 44/36, the SELECT scale, not DateInput's 48/44), a standalone menu item, a Day cell, Calendar pickers, Line and Bar charts, a Scrollbar and a stepper. `npm run check:axes` lists them as a backlog rather than failing on them.

Tabs shipped at 44 where Figma draws 42 — a CSS border taking layout space where a stroke does not. Fixed by shaving the container's vertical padding from 4 to 3. Worth a designer confirming the visual inset still reads right, since the padding no longer matches the file literally even though the height now does.

`triggerButtonVariant` — Figma turns the Select trigger into a Button and XUI's is always a field, so an "Actions" control reads as an input where the product draws a filled button. Already on the not-built list. (The other half of this, the panel truncating against a short trigger, is fixed: Select gained `menuWidth`.)

The Compact variants carry an "Error Message" text layer, but it sits inside a HIDDEN ancestor in every variant and is filled #666666 — a placeholder grey, not an error colour. So XUI has no error state for FileUpload and Figma does not actually define one. Is an error state intended? A CSV import will want one.

notBuilt.why: The first changes how the list renders; the other two turn the trigger into a Button. Both want their own pass.
Drawn in the reference library; not yet reconciled with XUI's own Drawer.
The mobile treatment for a data table has not been designed in XUI.

beyondFigma.note: Figma draws `bottom` hugging its content only. Approved with the body scrolling once content outgrows the height.
On by default. No gesture library; it yields to text fields and to a scrolled body.

beyondFigma.what: Escape, scrim click and body scroll-lock
beyondFigma.note: Dismissal is an interaction spec, and Figma carries none. Decided here.
None of the three Figma screens has one; it exists so the component covers what KoinX's InfoComponent already ships.
Figma draws the two buttons side by side at 1440 only.

beyondFigma.what: the rail stays put while content scrolls
beyondFigma.note: A static frame cannot express scroll behaviour.

overrides.what: 16px sides on the header and body
overrides.note: XUI 1416:47417 lays header content out at x=12 in all eight frames. 16 was chosen from a measurement of production, so the title shares a left edge with the body text. The one place this component knowingly departs from the file.
